asked.text:
Next: anti-churn fixes (user-approved). In the last Sonnet replay JNJ was bought and sold 8 times and OKE, MO, PEP, WMT, COP and LOW also flipped; the full-exit-only cooldown didn't catch partial trims and top-ups.
1. Make portfolio rebalancing weekly (a configurable day) by default. Daily runs still do monitoring and alerts, and may only trade on hard triggers: a risk-limit breach, stop or drawdown rules, a material cited event (8-K, earnings, guidance) that changes the thesis, or a new high-conviction entry above a threshold.
2. Cooldown of N sessions (default 10) after ANY trade on a name, in either direction, unless a hard trigger fires.
3. Thesis-change gate: a trade on an existing holding must cite what changed since the last decision on that name (new fact_refs dated after it). Otherwise it's blocked and logged.
4. A minimum trade size (dollars and % of book) so tiny $1 trims don't happen; the no-trade band applies to drift.
5. Add a turnover and round-trip metric to the replay report, plus a test that recreates the JNJ flip pattern and asserts it's blocked.
Also, EIA is skipped permanently (the user can't register); make it a silent optional skip rather than a warn. FRED_API_KEY and CENSUS_API_KEY are now set on the box. Make sure the FRED and Census refreshes write dated point-in-time rows and that data-audit reports them. Pick a sensible default series set relevant to the AI supply chain (power and electricity, industrial production, semis, construction, rates, inflation, labor). Tests and ruff must pass; export the tarball. No paid replay.

Next: anti-churn fixes (user-approved). In the last Sonnet replay JNJ was bought and sold 8 times and OKE, MO, PEP, WMT, COP and LOW also flipped; the full-exit-only cooldown didn't catch partial trims and top-ups.
1. Make portfolio rebalancing weekly (a configurable day) by default. Daily runs still do monitoring and alerts, and may only trade on hard triggers: a risk-limit breach, stop or drawdown rules, a material cited event (8-K, earnings, guidance) that changes the thesis, or a new high-conviction entry above a threshold.
2. Cooldown of N sessions (default 10) after ANY trade on a name, in either direction, unless a hard trigger fires.
3. Thesis-change gate: a trade on an existing holding must cite what changed since the last decision on that name (new fact_refs dated after it). Otherwise it's blocked and logged.
4. A minimum trade size (dollars and % of book) so tiny $1 trims don't happen; the no-trade band applies to drift.
5. Add a turnover and round-trip metric to the replay report, plus a test that recreates the JNJ flip pattern and asserts it's blocked.
Also, EIA is skipped permanently (the user can't register); make it a silent optional skip rather than a warn. FRED_API_KEY and CENSUS_API_KEY are now set on the box. Make sure the FRED and Census refreshes write dated point-in-time rows and that data-audit reports them. Pick a sensible default series set relevant to the AI supply chain (power and electricity, industrial production, semis, construction, rates, inflation, labor). Tests and ruff must pass; export the tarball. No paid replay.
